sections.hypothesis: stablecoin-vol-hold on BTC and ETH, traded forward through Kestrel on Binance's Spot Testnet, (a) behaves exactly as the backtest model says it should, and (b) beats each coin held at the same average exposure on data that didn't exist when it was designed.
sections.rationale: On watch, not pursue (Luke, 2026-11-15): it beat holding at the same exposure on both coins (Sharpe 0.87 vs 0.74 BTC, 0.68 ETH, 2018-25) but failed luck, walk-forward and drawdown. Luke asked on 2026-11-22 to judge it forward rather than search history further: forward data costs no trials and can't be fitted. It is the one watched idea with a reason unrelated to price trend (new dollars arriving as stablecoins), so it may be a second bet rather than more of the trend bet the pursued strategies share (findings 16); the overlap is reported at review. Statistical power is low and said now: at a Sharpe near 0.87, about two years are needed for 90% confidence that the true Sharpe is above zero (ignoring fat tails, which make it longer), so 395 days can catch a failure or a broken pipe, not prove an edge. Its holdout result (notes holdout-stablecoin-vol-hold-btc and -eth) is reported beside it and decides nothing here. The supply comes from DefiLlama each run, appended only (saved days are never rewritten), so the replay reads what the account knew. The testnet proves the plumbing; the strategy is judged on the model replay at real Binance prices.
sections.rules: Two accounts: kestrel paper open scs-btc --symbol BTCUSDT --strategy stablecoin-vol-hold --research <this note> --venue testnet --cash 330, and the same for scs-eth on ETHUSDT; then kestrel paper schedule for each (hourly at 10 past, with alerts). Default settings, daily bars, the [risk] limits in kestrel.toml. Each run refreshes the coin and the stablecoin supply and refuses to decide a bar with a missing input. The accounts share the testnet login with the others; reconciliation requires the exchange to hold at least what every ledger says. Runs 395 days from its first decision, reviewed with the others every 3 months. Interim reviews report; only the 6-month check can end it, and only for failure.
sections.falsification: Plumbing, at every review: any decision that differs from the model is a bug, fixed before the test continues; missed days under 5% of days handled; a refusal for missing supply is a plumbing event to investigate. Early failure, at 182 days only: if a coin's model replay is behind that coin held at its average exposure on both Sharpe and return, Claude recommends stopping that coin and Luke decides. Strategy, at 395 days, each coin: the model replay must (1) have a probabilistic Sharpe of at least 90%, (2) beat the coin held at its average exposure, by Sharpe if holding's Sharpe is positive and by return if not, and (3) keep its worst drawdown no deeper than 50%. Passing would support a move from watch to pursue, Luke's call; failing any one means Claude recommends drop and Luke decides.
sections.parameters: vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the defaults; never changed during the test).
sections.costs: Modelled at kestrel.toml's costs; testnet fills pay their own fees, so tracking shows fees apart from the model. Paper trading is not a trial: nothing is chosen from it.
